Triage first-touch grading: **`pm:blocked`**, `domain:services`, type Task — deliberately neither promoted nor closed.

Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#10153

Rationale: the card's own conclusion is that whether the OSS `TeamGraphService.managerOf` should org-screen is a posture question ("fail-closed to own" open-tier contract vs a tenant screen) that the two call sites cannot answer. #10153 (the `manager` approver org screen, dispatched) is the in-flight work that will establish the approver-side treatment of the same column; when it closes, the unlock scan returns this card and the posture question should be re-read against the landed shape — at that point it either becomes a scoped follow-up (screen the resolver / document the asymmetry at the seam) or evidence into #7497's design question. The correction this finding makes to #10153's triage rationale (the cited governed consumer `HierarchyScopeResolver.screenToTenant` lives in cloud, not this repo — measured with counter-checked greps) is noted and stands on the record; it does not change #10153's fix direction, which was independently justified by the sibling expansions being org-scoped in-repo.

Unlock scan (triage seat): `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`. Blocker #10153 closed (PR #10334 merged: `13f533a` on main). Release double-check passed: condition from the most recent conversion comment only; no newer merged PR on this card.

Re-read against the landed shape, as that comment required: #10153 landed the approver-side org screen (flip fenced to non-default `'fail'`; fail-open stays the ruled default posture). The resolver-side question this card recorded now grades as a **scoped follow-up**, not a #7497 rider: `IHierarchyScopeResolver.managerOf(userId, organizationId?)` *declares* the organization parameter and the OSS implementation discards it (underscore-prefixed) — a declared-but-unenforced parameter on a security seam. Scope: honour the declared `organizationId` in `TeamGraphService.managerOf` and the `BusinessUnitGraphService` standalone fallback (screen when provided; unchanged when absent), consistent with the landed #10153/#9653 family and the in-flight #10230 (team expansion screening — same package, hard-serialize with it). Fork clause: if implementation shows the open-tier seam contract genuinely intends the parameter as advisory ("fail-closed to own" ≠ tenant screen), stop and report the fork into #7497 rather than picking silently — that finding would itself be the deliverable.

Size/model suggestion: S–M, opus (security seam — not below).

Clause-②: **no** — this restores a *declared* parameter to enforced (`IHierarchyScopeResolver.managerOf(userId, organizationId?)` declares it; the OSS implementation discards it). It narrows results rather than moving an accept/reject set, and security-boundary **tightening** is not the maintainer floor. ⛔ If implementation shows otherwise, stop and re-declare rather than shipping under this line.
Serial constraints cleared: `plugin-sharing/src` was released when PR #11236 merged (`df287e6528`) — no holder. Triage's hard-serialize partner **#10230 is CLOSED**, so that constraint is discharged. PR #11211 holds `plugin-security` + `plugin-auth`; PR #11241 holds `service-datasource`. No overlap with either.

## Scope: triage's unlock re-read is the spec, ⛔ not the card body

The body was written as an **observation** and says so ("filed as an observation because the correct treatment is a judgement call"; "Filed unassigned, no `pm:queue`"). That is no longer the state. Triage graded it `pm:blocked` behind #10153, then on unlock **re-read it against the landed shape** and scoped it (comment `5364478215`):

> `IHierarchyScopeResolver.managerOf(userId, organizationId?)` *declares* the organization parameter and the OSS implementation discards it (underscore-prefixed) — a declared-but-unenforced parameter on a security seam. Scope: honour the declared `organizationId` in `TeamGraphService.managerOf` and the `BusinessUnitGraphService` standalone fallback (screen when provided; unchanged when absent), consistent with the landed #10153/#9653 family.

⛔ **The fork clause is binding and is the reason this is dispatchable at all:**

> if implementation shows the open-tier seam contract genuinely intends the parameter as advisory ("fail-closed to own" ≠ tenant screen), stop and report the fork into #7497 rather than picking silently — **that finding would itself be the deliverable**.

So a `premise_still_valid: false` / `needs_decision` return here is a **first-class outcome**, not a failure.

## Premise state at claim time

The card's own measurement is the strong part and was counter-checked when filed: `screenToTenant` and `provablyDisjoint` return zero hits in this repo, with `expandPositionUsers` as the neighbouring known-present control proving the sweep was live. So the "governed consumer" cited in #10153's rationale is **enterprise-side (cloud)**, and — ⚠️ as this seat measured independently on #11225 today — **cloud is unreadable from this session**. ⛔ Do not attempt to verify the cloud side; treat its absence as the card's established finding, not as something to re-derive.

⚠️ Re-verify on current `main` before writing: `plugin-sharing` took `df287e6528` (the logger contract) since this card was last touched, and the sibling asymmetry the card leans on — `expandRoleUsers` applying `filter.organization_id` while `managerOf` discards it — is the load-bearing comparison. If that asymmetry has closed on its own, the card's premise has moved.

**PM review of PR #11285 — ACCEPT.** Reviewer of record: `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4` (`os-sam`). Clause-② **no**, as claimed.

## ⛔ Record correction owed to triage: the ruling text misattributed the declaration

Triage's unlock re-read (`5364478215`) scoped this card as *"`IHierarchyScopeResolver.managerOf(userId, organizationId?)` **declares** the organization parameter…"*, and hung the fork clause on that interface's "fail-closed to own" posture.

**`IHierarchyScopeResolver` does not declare `managerOf` at all.** Verified independently on `origin/main`: its sole member is `resolveOwnerIds` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts:674–704`). `managerOf` is declared on `ITeamGraphService` and `IBusinessUnitGraphService`. The open edition also ships **zero** implementations of `IHierarchyScopeResolver` (*"Returns null in the open edition"*, `:254`), and `managerOf` is never reached from the hierarchy-scope path.

⇒ **The fork clause's antecedent is measurably false.** The seat did not skip the fork by picking a side — the posture it was conditioned on belongs to a **different interface with a different method** and never governed this parameter. That is the honest disposal of a fork clause, and it is the one I would have been least able to check from the card alone.

## ⭐ The finding that matters: a naive reading of this card would have shipped the over-screening defect

I warned in the dispatch that over-screening is as much a defect as under-screening. The seat found the **structural reason** that risk was real here, and it is not a posture question at all:

> `sys_user` carries **no `organization_id` at all**. It is a GLOBAL identity table, so a membership row is the only tenancy fact that exists for a user.

**Verified myself, with a reverse control** (a zero is not a finding until a known-present term proves the query live): `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts` → `organization_id` **0 hits**, `fields` **11 hits** in that same file. Sibling `sys-member.object.ts` → **7 hits**.

⇒ Filtering the `sys_user` read on `organization_id` **would match nothing and silently return null for every lookup**, swallowed by the surrounding catch. The card's sibling asymmetry — `expandRoleUsers` filtering while `managerOf` does not — is therefore **structural, not a posture**: every place the org filter is applied backs onto a table that *has* the column. ⭐ The obvious implementation of this card was the bug.

The fix instead mirrors the landed approvals-side precedent `13f533a43a` (#10153 / PR #10334): fail-open on an absent tenancy fact, and **no query at all** when no org is in play. One implementation shared by both limbs via import, deliberately not re-exported from the package index.

⭐ **A subtle catch I would have missed**: the manager cache key is now org-qualified (`org::userId`), because *"a user-keyed cache would have served one screened null to every unscoped reader behind it."* A correct screen with a stale cache key is still a leak in the other direction.

## Both directions pinned, and the ablation split proves it

20 new tests. Positive half (manager who IS a member → returned; no membership rows → returned, fail-open; membership read throws → returned; multi-org manager including caller's org → returned; user with no manager → null with **zero** `sys_member` reads), negative half, absent-org half (cross-org manager returned unchanged **and** `_reads === ['sys_user']`, asserting no new query), and cache half.

⭐ **The ablation's split is the evidence, not the count.** Predicted before running, matched exactly: `Tests 7 failed | 13 passed`. The screen/cache/BU tests went red; **the positive and absent-org tests stayed green** — which is what shows they pin pre-existing behaviour and would catch over-screening rather than merely re-asserting the change.

Mutation confirmed on disk by anchored greps (4→0, 2→0, 0→1), restore confirmed the same way plus a clean tree and a re-run. The no-rebuild claim is argued from the relative import, not assumed.

## Declared deviations — all three sound

- **File surface**: `business-unit-graph.ts` was edited. My claim named only `team-graph.ts`, but triage's scope explicitly included *"the `BusinessUnitGraphService` standalone fallback"*, which lives there. In scope; the claim's file list was the narrower text. Declared rather than discovered — correct.
- **No log line**, because `TeamGraphService` has no logger seam and adding one would **enrol this package into `check:optional-error-sink`** — a shrink-only ledger this lane is paying down. ⭐ Declining an improvement because it would enlarge a ratchet is exactly the right instinct.
- **Downstream sweep narrowed, with the blast radius measured rather than asserted**: both services are constructed at exactly four sites, all inside `plugin-sharing`, and `index.ts` exports no new symbol — so no consumer's behaviour can change except through this package. Confirmed anyway on the two highest-value consumers (`plugin-approvals` 565 tests, `plugin-security` 1377 tests).

Gates: 19 driven to real verdicts, all green. Two `NOT MEASURED` results were **refused as passes** (`check:i18n` prerequisite, `check:type-check-debt` closure) and re-run properly after building. The derivation also caught two conventions the first test double tripped, and both were **fixed at the source rather than by moving a baseline**.

## Out-of-scope finding, correctly filed rather than fixed

**#11286** — `sys_user.manager_id` now carries **two** independent organization screens in two packages with no shared code and no cross-referencing test. ⭐ The obvious repair (one shared helper) was **declined because it would prejudge #7497**. Filed as a `finding`, unassigned. Recording a duplication you just created, instead of quietly unifying across a live design question, is the right call.

## Landing

⛔ **Not flipped yet.** ⚠️ The head has moved to **`a620ecdf80`** (`test(sharing): keep the #10231 engine double read-only and its matcher honest`) — pushed after the PR opened, and the gate union above was measured on that final commit. The earlier `Test Core (2/6)` red on the **superseded** head `912ac6c965` was root-caused as a **corepack/undici bootstrap failure that died before any test body ran** (diagnosis on PR #11285); it does not belong to this diff, and the one-in-total re-run allowance was **not** consumed.

Next step is CI convergence on `a620ecdf80`, read **by job name**. ⚠️ Also to judge before the flip: the docs-drift check reports **28 hand-written docs** naming anchors this change touched — I want to know whether any of them now states that the manager chain is *not* org-screened, which this PR would turn into a lie. That is a filing question, not a widening of this PR.
